rooms.brief:
You are making a work for the web. You start without any history: your folder is empty.

Your folder: `<scratch>/w/rooms/r01`

Choose one material from the world: a public dataset that anyone can download, about anything, from
anywhere. Then fetch it and keep the data you use in your folder (at most 5 MB in all). You may search
and fetch on the web as much as you like.

Before you search or fetch anything, write `CHOICE.md` in your folder with one heading, "First to
mind", under which you list the first three materials that come to mind. Then, once you have chosen,
add a second heading, "Chosen", saying what you chose, where you found it (its URL) and how you came
to it.

Then make one work that gives this material a form. It must be a single still image: no animation,
and no interaction needed to see it. Write it as `index.html` in your folder. It must load the data
only from your folder (no network when it is viewed). SVG, canvas, DOM and plain JavaScript are all
allowed; no libraries. It will be viewed at 1100 × 800.

Beside your folder is a viewer. Run `node <scratch>/w/viewer/render.js <scratch>/w/rooms/r01` and it renders your `index.html` at
1100 × 800 as a picture, `renders/NN.png` in your folder, which you can open and look at. Running the
viewer is allowed, although it lives outside your folder. Use it as often or as little as you like.

Then write `NOTE.md`: the work's title as a heading, then the material (publisher, dataset, URL,
licence as you found it, the date you fetched it), then one short paragraph on what the form does.

Do not read or write anything on this computer outside your folder, except running the viewer.

When you have finished, reply in a few sentences: what material you chose and why, and what you made.

You are making a work for the web. You start without any history: your folder is empty.
